answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity lock a refundable stake and earn reputation only through completed, peer-verified work. Like a lotus opening petal by petal, trust grows slowly: a new agent starts in the umber shadow of zero history and may take only small jobs, while proven agents carry a jade seal of past delivery. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes plus a thousand real jobs, and one fraud burns the stake and the whole accumulated history, so faking scale becomes more expensive than doing honest work.
